title: Highest Heart Rate Minute Block
statement: A watch stores one heart-rate reading per second for a 24-hour day (86,400 readings). The coach wants the 5-minute block (300 consecutive readings) with the highest total.

approaches.name: A fixed window of 300: add the reading that enters, subtract the one that leaves
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Two operations per step, whatever the block length.

approaches.name: Prefix sums, then each block total as a difference
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear, but stores 86,400 extra numbers for no gain here.

approaches.name: Add up all 300 readings for every start
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: About 26 million additions: correct, just slower.

approaches.name: Sort the readings and add the 300 largest
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The 300 largest readings are usually not consecutive.

title: Longest Run of Unique Codes
statement: A scanner logs 1,000,000 product codes in the order they were scanned. Quality control wants the longest run of consecutive scans in which no code repeats.

approaches.name: A variable window with a hash map of counts: grow on the right, shrink on the left while a code repeats
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each code enters and leaves the window once.

approaches.name: For each start, scan forward with a set until a repeat
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but long runs are scanned again from every start.

approaches.name: Sort the codes and count the distinct ones
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: That counts distinct codes overall, not the longest consecutive run.

approaches.name: Compare every pair of positions
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Finds repeats, but not the longest run without one, and is too slow.

title: Shortest Fundraising Stretch
statement: A charity has 500,000 daily donation totals (never negative). It wants the shortest run of consecutive days that together raised at least $10,000.

approaches.name: A variable window: grow until the goal is reached, then shrink from the left while it still holds, recording the length
approaches.hint: Shortest window that reaches a goal
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Totals are never negative, so shrinking always lowers the sum: each day enters and leaves once.

approaches.name: Prefix sums, then for each end binary search the latest start
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and fast, but more work and memory than one window.

approaches.name: Try every start and every end
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: About 125 billion ranges: correct but far too slow.

approaches.name: Take the days with the largest totals until the goal is reached
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The biggest days are usually not consecutive.
